questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to write good headlines
Why people stop using social media
How to go fishing
Online content made to make people angry so that creators earn money
questions.why: They explore rage bait – online content designed to make you angry – and how it makes money.

questions.q: What is clickbait used for, according to Phil?
options: To give people true news quickly
To grab people's attention and make them read more
To stop people from reading too many stories about celebrities
To sell computer software
questions.why: Phil says headlines like these are used to grab your attention and make you read more.

questions.q: How does rage bait make money for its creator?
options: People pay to read the content
The creator sells the angry comments
Angry reactions and sharing increase traffic, which earns money
Advertisers pay the creator only when people leave positive comments
questions.why: People comment angrily or share it, which increases internet traffic and makes money for the creator.

questions.q: According to marketing strategist Andrea Jones, why do some creators do anything for views?
options: Because more views mean more pay, even if the reactions are negative
Because they enjoy making people angry
Because their clients force them to
Because positive views are much too hard to get on today's social media
questions.why: She says the more views they get, the more they get paid, 'even if those views are negative'.

questions.q: What is the difference between a 'hook' and rage bait, according to Andrea?
options: A hook is longer than rage bait
Rage bait is more honest than a hook because it shows real feelings
A hook shows the content honestly, but rage bait is manipulative
There is no real difference
questions.why: She says a hook accurately reflects the content and comes from trust, while rage bait is manipulative.

questions.q: According to Dr William Brady, how do influencers get more people to see their content?
options: By paying for adverts
By posting only at night
By making calm, balanced videos that people are happy to share with friends
By using the biases in our psychology, which algorithms then boost
questions.why: He says they exploit our psychological biases, and algorithms amplify that content.

questions.q: Why, according to Beth, does emotional content grab our attention?
options: Because listening to emotions has been important in human evolution
Because we are all addicted to phones
Because emotional content online is almost always true and trustworthy
Because we can't control what we read
questions.why: She says listening to our emotions has been vital to the evolution of the human species.

questions.q: What does Phil suggest about sharing outrageous content?
options: It helps stop the creator
It can make things worse and make the creator richer
It is the best way to complain and to make the creator stop posting
It has no effect at all
questions.why: He says by sharing it you might be making things worse while also making the creator richer.
